title.narrative: Dushanbe-Kyrgyz Border Road Rehabilitation Project, Phase II (Tajikistan)

description.narrative: The project of L2196-TAJ was approved in 2005, as a government priority. It aims to rehabilitate the road from Dushanbe to the border with the Kyrgyz Republic - part of the CAREC Transport corridors 3 and 5. The supplementary grant will reinforce that project's development impact, outcome and outputs. It will complete the entire Dushanbe-Kyrgyz border road (the road). The supplementary grant original outputs are (i) the rehabilitated road section from Obigarm to Nurobod (km 95-140), (ii) the repaired emergency bypass road at km 110-112, (iii) the improved central section from Nurobod to Nimich (km 140-217) and (iv) the upgraded border section at Karamyk. This grant financing will improve 127-km of the road and 7-km of the bypass road.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Original project outcome reinforced; improved access to markets and social services.

By 2012, daily international freight traffic on the project corridor increased to 177 trucks (baseline: 10 trucks in 2006) Progress/Status: Daily international freight traffic in 2012 was on average 82 trucks per day. Data Source: National economic and social statistics, and MOTC's surveys and statistics Actual value:

By 2012, travel time between Dushanbe and the Kyrgyz border reduced to 7 hours (baseline: 10 hours in 2006) Progress/Status: Travel time from the border to Dushanbe redcued to 7 hours in 2012. Data Source: National economic and social statistics, and MOTC's surveys and statistics Actual value:

By 2012, domestic traffic on the project corridor increased to 750 AADT (baseline: 250 AADT in 2006) Progress/Status: AADT counted on the main road was recorded 2,071 vehicles in 2012. Data Source: National economic and social statistics, and MOTC's surveys and statistics Actual value:

By 2012, traffic accidents on the project corridor reduced to 14 accidents per 750 AADT(baseline: 14 accidents per 250 AADT in 2006) Progress/Status: Traffic accidents on the main road were 14 per 2,187 AADT in 2012. Data Source: National economic and social statistics, and MOTC's surveys and statistics Actual value:
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Rehabilitation of 127 km of the project corridor Indicator: By 2011, 77km of the section from Nurobad to Nimich (km140-km217) rehabilitated Progress/Status: Rehabilitated 72.9 km of the section at km 140-217. Data Source: MOTC's quarterly monitoring and evaluation reports and progress reports Actual value:

Output: 1. Rehabilitation of 127 km of the project corridor Indicator: By 2012, 41 km of the road section from Obigarm to Nurobad (km95-km140) upgraded Progress/Status: Rehabilitated 27 km of the section at km 95-140 (12 km at km 95-107 and 15 km in total at km 112-140). Data Source: MOTC's quarterly monitoring and evaluation reports and progress reports Actual value:

Output: 2. Improvement of 7 km of the emergency bypass road Indicator: By 2011, 7 km of emergency bypass road (km110-km112) improved Progress/Status: Constructed emergency bypass in 2011. Data Source: MOTC's quarterly monitoring and evaluation reports and progress reports Actual value:

Output: 3. Regular maintenance system implemented at Karamyk Section (km 337-346) Indicator: By 2012, equipment for regular maintenance procured and mobilized Progress/Status: All the equipment were procured, delivered and assembled at the designated sites, in accordance with the requirement in the contract. The entire works were completed in June 2013. Data Source: MOTC's website Baseline year: 2009 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2009 Baseline value: N Target year: 2012 Target value: Y
